title: HER2 ISH in Breast Cancer: The 2018 ASCO/CAP Groups
summary: Count HER2 and CEP17 signals in at least 20 tumour nuclei, assign the five ASCO/CAP 2018 ISH groups from copy number and ratio, and resolve groups 2–4 with concurrent IHC and a blinded recount.

reviewer.note: Teaches Ch. 78 Hit 1 (first lesson for Ch. 78). The ASCO/CAP guideline itself was not accessible; its 2018 rules are taught as summarized in Wang 2019, Gupta 2019 and Nagarjun 2022. Nuance: the reviewer lists Group 3 (ratio < 2.0, ≥ 6.0/cell) as “positive”; under 2018 rules it requires concurrent IHC (IHC 0/1+ → negative). The 2023 ASCO/CAP update (HER2-low reporting) was not read.

objectives: Explain what dual-probe HER2 ISH counts.
Resolve groups 2–4 using concurrent IHC and recount.

scenes.title: Ratio 2.3 — positive?
scenes.altText: An invented breast cancer HER2 dual-probe FISH result, IHC 2+ (equivocal): 20 nuclei counted; average HER2 signals 3.4 per cell; average CEP17 1.5 per cell; HER2/CEP17 ratio 2.3. A student says “ratio over 2 = amplified.” Question token: “Positive, negative — or does it need more work?”

cues.text: A breast cancer has an equivocal HER2 immunohistochemistry score of 2 plus, so dual-probe FISH is done.
In 20 nuclei: on average 3.4 HER2 signals and 1.5 chromosome 17 centromere signals per cell. The ratio is 2.3.
A student calls it amplified because the ratio is above 2. Is it?

scenes.title: What dual-probe ISH counts
scenes.altText: Probe card: dual-probe ISH labels the HER2 gene and the chromosome 17 centromere (CEP17) in each tumour nucleus; signals are counted in at least 20 tumour cells. Two numbers come out: the average HER2 copy number per cell, and the HER2/CEP17 ratio. Schematic nuclei: normal (2 HER2, 2 CEP17); amplified (clusters of HER2, 2 CEP17); polysomy-like (3 HER2, 3 CEP17 — ratio 1.0 despite more copies).

cues.text: Dual-probe in situ hybridization labels two targets in each tumour nucleus: the HER2 gene and the centromere of chromosome 17, called CEP17.
Signals are counted in at least 20 tumour cells. That gives two numbers: the average HER2 copies per cell, and the ratio of HER2 to CEP17.
A normal nucleus has about two of each. An amplified nucleus has many HER2 signals for two centromeres.
The two numbers can disagree, so the 2018 ASCO and CAP guideline sorts results into five groups using both.

scenes.title: The five ISH groups
scenes.altText: Group table (ASCO/CAP 2018 as summarized by Wang 2019 and Gupta 2019). Group 1: ratio ≥ 2.0 and ≥ 4.0 HER2/cell → positive. Group 2: ratio ≥ 2.0 but < 4.0 HER2/cell → needs concurrent IHC review. Group 3: ratio < 2.0 but ≥ 6.0 HER2/cell → needs concurrent IHC review. Group 4: ratio < 2.0 and ≥ 4.0 but < 6.0 HER2/cell → needs concurrent IHC review. Group 5: ratio < 2.0 and < 4.0 HER2/cell → negative. Back to the hook: ratio 2.3 but 3.4 copies/cell = Group 2 — not automatically positive.

cues.text: Group 1: ratio of 2 or more and at least 4 HER2 copies per cell. Positive.
Group 5: ratio below 2 and fewer than 4 copies. Negative.
Group 2: ratio of 2 or more, but fewer than 4 copies. Group 3: ratio below 2, but 6 or more copies.
Group 4: ratio below 2, with 4 to just under 6 copies. Groups 2, 3 and 4 need the IHC result reviewed alongside before a final call.
Our case: ratio 2.3, but only 3.4 copies per cell. That is Group 2, not automatically positive.

scenes.title: Resolving groups 2–4 with IHC
scenes.altText: Work-up card (Gupta 2019; Nagarjun 2022): for ISH groups 2–4, review concurrent IHC on the same specimen. IHC 3+ → HER2 positive. IHC 0 or 1+ → HER2 negative. IHC 2+ → an additional observer, blinded to the first result, recounts at least 20 cells in the area of IHC 2+; if the recount still falls in group 2 or 4, the result is HER2 negative (with comment); group 3 with IHC 2+ after recount → positive. Data token (Wang 2019, 1,810 IHC-equivocal cases): applying 2018 rules reclassified all group 2 cases as negative and most group 4 cases as negative, slightly lowering the positive rate. Back to the hook: Group 2 with IHC 2+ → blinded recount of ≥ 20 cells; if still Group 2 → HER2 negative with a comment.

cues.text: For groups 2 to 4, review the immunohistochemistry on the same tumour. IHC 3 plus makes the case HER2 positive; IHC 0 or 1 plus makes it negative.
If IHC is 2 plus, a second observer, blinded to the first count, recounts at least 20 cells in the IHC 2 plus area.
If the recount still falls in group 2 or group 4, the result is reported as HER2 negative, with a comment.
In a study of 1,810 equivocal cases, the 2018 rules moved all group 2 cases and most group 4 cases to negative.
Our case: group 2 with IHC 2 plus needs a blinded recount. If it stays group 2, it is HER2 negative with a comment.

props.label: Hook: recount; if still Group 2 → HER2 negative + comment

scenes.title: Three classic traps
scenes.altText: Three trap cards: “Ratio ≥ 2.0 alone = HER2 positive” (✓ Group 2 has ratio ≥ 2.0 but < 4.0 copies/cell — needs IHC review); “≥ 6 copies = positive without IHC” (✓ Group 3 needs concurrent IHC: IHC 0/1+ → negative); “Count any 20 cells” (✓ count ≥ 20 invasive tumour nuclei, in the IHC 2+ area when recounting).

cues.text: Trap one: a ratio of 2 or more alone means positive. Group 2 has that ratio but fewer than 4 copies per cell, and needs IHC review.
Trap two: 6 or more copies means positive without IHC. Group 3 still needs the IHC result; IHC 0 or 1 plus makes it negative.
Trap three: count any 20 cells. Count at least 20 invasive tumour nuclei, and for a recount, in the IHC 2 plus area.

scenes.title: Two keys: 2 and 4
scenes.altText: Memory aid: “HER2 positive needs two keys — ratio 2 AND copies 4. One key only? Call the IHC.” Tokens: 2 + 4 = Group 1 · one key = Groups 2–4 → IHC · no keys = Group 5. A card lists where the aid breaks.

cues.text: Memory aid: HER2 positive needs two keys, a ratio of 2 and copies of 4. With only one key, call the IHC. With no keys, it is negative.
Where it breaks: Group 3 uses a copy threshold of 6, not 4; Group 4 has neither key but still needs IHC; and the 2023 guideline update adds reporting changes not covered here.

props.title: Where it breaks
lines: Group 4: no key but still IHC

scenes.title: Takeaway
scenes.altText: Two tokens: “Count ≥ 20 tumour nuclei · Group 1 (ratio ≥ 2 and ≥ 4/cell) positive · Group 5 (ratio < 2 and < 4/cell) negative”, “Groups 2–4 → concurrent IHC: 3+ positive, 0/1+ negative, 2+ blinded recount (groups 2 and 4 → negative with comment)”.

cues.text: Under the 2018 ASCO/CAP rules, HER2 ISH is positive outright only when the ratio is at least 2.0 with at least 4.0 copies per cell, and groups 2 to 4 are resolved with concurrent IHC and a blinded recount.

props.label: G2–4 → IHC: 3+ pos · 0/1+ neg · 2+ blinded recount (G2/G4 → neg)

explanation.what: Plain language: in breast cancer, a fluorescent DNA test counts copies of the HER2 gene and of a chromosome 17 marker in tumour cells; the two numbers together decide whether HER2-targeted drugs are appropriate, and borderline patterns are settled by looking at the protein stain. Scientific terms: dual-probe in situ hybridization (ISH/FISH), HER2 (ERBB2), CEP17, average HER2 copy number, HER2/CEP17 ratio, ISH groups 1–5, immunohistochemistry (IHC 0, 1+, 2+, 3+), blinded recount.
explanation.why: Gene amplification raises HER2 copies relative to chromosome 17. Copy number and ratio can disagree, so the guideline combines both, and uses protein expression (IHC) to decide discordant patterns.
explanation.measure: ≥ 20 tumour nuclei counted. Group 1: ratio ≥ 2.0, ≥ 4.0/cell → positive. Group 2: ratio ≥ 2.0, < 4.0/cell. Group 3: ratio < 2.0, ≥ 6.0/cell. Group 4: ratio < 2.0, ≥ 4.0 and < 6.0/cell. Group 5: ratio < 2.0, < 4.0/cell → negative. Groups 2–4: concurrent IHC — 3+ positive, 0/1+ negative, 2+ blinded recount of ≥ 20 cells; recount still group 2 or 4 → negative (Gupta 2019; Nagarjun 2022; Wang 2019).
explanation.differs: Ratio alone (pre-2018 practice) vs ratio plus copy number (2018 groups); definitive groups (1, 5) vs groups requiring IHC review (2–4).
explanation.examAngle: Expect: assigning an ISH group from numbers, whether ratio ≥ 2.0 with < 4.0 copies is positive, and what happens with IHC 2+ in groups 2–4.

mnemonic.explanation: Group 1 has both keys (positive); groups with one key need IHC review; group 5 has neither (negative).
mnemonic.limitation: Group 3 uses ≥ 6 copies; group 4 has neither key yet still needs IHC; the 2023 update is not covered.
